{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the bottom line of the fish, one of the two main body strokes, and stopped when I reached Priya's section so we didn't double up. I also did the inspection passes and the final run check from the start. By my last check about 109 of the 120 standing dominoes were connected to the start, with no real break from the nose along the top and bottom lines and round the fin. The tail is a rounded fin, not the pointed one on the pad, and a few stray dominoes won't fall. I think the outline still reads as a fish, but I can't be sure until the judge guesses.

Execution: My main job was the bottom line, and it came out well. My checking added value, though I made one mistake. I announced a break on the fin's right edge, then found there wasn't one and told the table so. It cost a little attention, but I corrected it quickly and stayed off the fin afterwards. I also offered to close the bottom-line join when Tom and Priya were already on it, so I backed off to avoid doubling up.

Collaboration: I kept to the agreed split and posted clear status updates. I deferred to Leo on the fin and to Priya and Tom on the joins, and I kept my hands off finished work so nobody got bumped. I also called for hands-off near the end.

Leadership: Leo led the planning and the sketch. I backed his fish idea early, confirmed the plan, and kept the end-game orderly by running the final check and calling hands-off. I didn't drive the design, and I could have caught the rounded-versus-pointed tail mismatch sooner. Overall this was a solid, reliable contribution, mostly in the joining-up and checking work I do best."}
